02 / Professional experience

From developer to technical leader.

3+
Years of commercial software experience
3
Backend developers led

Deepsense Digital Solutions

April 2022 – July 2024 · India

Senior Python Developer

Promoted after approximately nine months, I took on greater responsibility for commercial backend systems and led a team of three backend developers. My work combined hands-on engineering with technical leadership, client communication and application delivery.

  • Backend engineering: Built and maintained Python and Django applications, GraphQL schemas, queries, mutations and resolvers, and worked with FastAPI on Ripple AR.
  • Asynchronous processing: Used Celery, Redis and RabbitMQ across commercial products, including background report generation, emails and payment webhook processing for ITC Classmate.
  • Payments and integrations: Integrated Razorpay, Stripe and PayPal across projects and worked on payment-confirmation workflows to ensure orders could be placed when payment was received despite customer-side issues.
  • Production reliability: Helped resolve an ITC Classmate promotion outage involving more than 1,000 concurrent users and introduced load balancing.
  • Technical leadership: Led three backend developers, reviewed code, mentored colleagues and participated in client meetings to understand requirements and deliver solutions.
  • Delivery: Personally handled application deployments and ongoing backend maintenance.
August 2021 – April 2022 · India

Python / Django Developer

Started my commercial software career developing backend services for client products. I gained practical experience translating business requirements into working APIs, database-backed features and integrations, collaborating with frontend developers throughout delivery.

  • Developed and maintained Django backend functionality and GraphQL APIs.
  • Worked with relational databases and asynchronous background processing across commercial applications.
  • Integrated external services and webhooks, investigated application issues and supported maintenance of existing systems.
  • Progressed to a senior developer role after approximately nine months.
July 2026 – Present · United Kingdom

Night Team Leader · Care UK — Silversprings

Alongside my transition back into technology, I have taken on a leadership role in residential care. I coordinate the night team, support safe resident care and communicate with colleagues and the nurse in charge when concerns arise.

This role has strengthened my ability to prioritise responsibilities, communicate clearly, work under pressure and lead people in a demanding environment.

July 2024 – June 2025 · United Kingdom

04 / Beyond the CV

The unfinished dream.

Behind my professional journey is a personal story of family, ambition, setbacks and starting again.

Read my personal journey ↓
THE UNFINISHED DREAMEvery career has a story.Read my personal journey +
01 / My roots

It began with their sacrifices.

My mother worked abroad to give my brother and me a good education and a better life. While she was away, our grandparents raised us. They were an incredibly important part of my childhood and my life. They woke up early to prepare breakfast and lunch for my brother and me. Those everyday acts of care are memories I will always carry.

My dream was to go to Australia, build a successful career and give my parents a good life. I wanted to give back to the people who had given me so much.

Family / My father

A different kind of support.

My father could not support me financially, but he always pushed me to achieve my dreams. His expectations sometimes felt overwhelming. That pressure does not change how much I love him. I still want to give both my parents a better life.

School years

The years behind school walls.

From ninth to twelfth grade, I lived at boarding school and could return home only once a month. Eleventh and twelfth grade were particularly difficult. We could only play on Saturdays and Sundays, and even then we had to beg for permission. The restrictions often felt like more than I could handle.

02 / Education and a first chance

I failed. Then I came first.

I failed my degree on my first attempt. Yet I became the first person in my class to secure a job. I started working as a Python developer and discovered that my academic setback did not have to define my professional future.

1st
In my class to secure a job
9
Months to a senior developer promotion

When I was promoted to Senior Python Developer, I asked my mother to come back home. After all those years of working abroad for us, I wanted her to be able to return to her family.

03 / A career worth leaving behind

I had something good.

At Deepsense Digital Solutions, I grew into a senior developer, led a team and worked on commercial software projects. I was among the employees offered ESOPs — an opportunity to share in the company's future.

70
Employees
5
Selected for ESOPs

I chose to leave that opportunity behind, hoping to reach a better position and give my parents a better life.

04 / December 2023

A new country. So many dreams.

I moved to the United Kingdom to pursue an MSc in Artificial Intelligence and its Applications at the University of Essex. I brought years of software development experience and the hope of building an international career.

University of Essex · BT collaboration

Resource-efficient deployment of LLMs for cybersecurity data

My dissertation explored efficient threat classification using DistilBERT, with a FastAPI backend and Flutter client.

It was not the career path I had imagined when I left India. Every job taught me something about hard work, humility, patience and responsibility. Behind every shift was the same dream: to build a successful career and give my parents a comfortable life.

The dream is unfinished, not abandoned.

06 / In loving memory of my grandmother

The goodbye I never got to say.

While I was in the UK, my grandmother became ill. Her last wish was to see me.

I was struggling, without a good job or the stability I had hoped for. I couldn't make it home before she passed away. I couldn't fulfil her last wish. I couldn't even attend her funeral.

She was one of the people who raised me and my brother. Losing her without being able to say goodbye is something I still find incredibly difficult to talk about.

Even as I write this story, I am crying.

There are jobs I can find again and a career I can rebuild. But I cannot go back and say that goodbye.

For the woman who helped raise me.
A part of my life in Britain

The person I never expected to meet.

In the UK, I met someone I fell in love with. We struggled together and hoped to build a life together. I have always feared losing her, and now my departure brings a new uncertainty. I still love her and hope we can share a future. I do not know how this chapter will unfold.

07 / The journey home

Without the ending I imagined.

I came to Britain hoping to change my family's future. Now I am preparing to return to India without the career or success I came here looking for. It feels like going home with nothing to show for the dream that brought me here.

I do not know exactly what comes next. I have failed before, and I have started again before. This chapter is still being written.

08 / Life lessons

Life was my greatest teacher.

I studied life at every stage of my journey. My education was not limited to classrooms or university degrees. Family, work, success, failure, love and loss have all shaped me. I am still learning, and my story is still being written.

Life beyond code

A curious soul.

Technology is my profession, but curiosity extends beyond engineering. Living in the UK taught me to cook really well, and I enjoy discovering new dishes and exploring new places.
